items.title: Collapsing a fibre of a proper family onto a separated finite-type target forces the whole family near the base point to factor through a finite subspace
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a commutative triangle X -> Y -> B of spaces over S with X -> B proper, Y -> B separated locally of finite type, and either (3a) the image of |X_k| -> |Y_k| finite or (3b) the image of the fibre over b in |Y| finite with B decent, there is an open B' through b through which X_{B'} -> Y_{B'} factors via a closed Z finite over B'. The retained proof: take Z the scheme-theoretic image of h; proper-pushforward lemmas make X -> Z surjective and Z -> B proper; the two fibre finiteness hypotheses make Z -> B quasi-finite at every point over b (Decent Spaces, conditions-on-fibre-and-qf); the in-source proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood lemma (this wave's L16242) turns that into finiteness over an open neighbourhood. The author's slogan: collapsing a fibre of a proper family forces nearby ones to collapse too. Retained author proof at lines 7960-7978.
